narrative:
On September 7, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing clearance rate of 48.5%, taking up 1,400 of 2,884 scheduled matters across 44 judges. This marks a notable improvement in both volume and disposal efficiency compared to recent sessions, surpassing the 35.6% hearing rate on September 3 (849 heard of 2,386), 41.2% on September 1 (1,038 heard of 2,520), and 44.6% on August 31 (960 heard of 2,153).

Bench throughput varied significantly across halls. Justice C.M. Poonacha led individual productivity, hearing 125 of 162 scheduled cases (77.2%). Strong clearance rates were also achieved by Justice H.P. Sandesh at 82.1% (46 of 56) and Justice V. Srishananda, who disposed of 113 matters across two cause lists (clearing 84.0% of a 50-case list and 61.2% of a 116-case list). Conversely, severe docket congestion suppressed conversion in Hall 7, where Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad heard 47 cases across two lists while a third list of 281 scheduled matters was entirely unaddressed.

Procedural stage analysis indicates that early and procedural listings converted most reliably. Admission matters reached a 62.8% hearing rate (395 of 629), followed closely by preliminary hearings at 61.8% and orders at 58.8% (442 of 752). In contrast, complex stages moved slowly: final hearings registered a 32.5% conversion rate (215 of 662)—an improvement over 22.8% on September 3—while further hearings converted at just 13.6% (53 of 389).

By case type, Writ Petitions dominated the docket with 1,380 scheduled filings, achieving a 44.4% hearing rate, higher than the 31.4% observed on September 3. Criminal Petitions demonstrated the strongest clearance among high-volume categories at 65.9% (222 of 337), while Miscellaneous First Appeals and Regular Second Appeals achieved 52.7% and 40.8%, respectively.
